correctness.rationale: Exact equilibrium elimination gives a positive-denominator rational response, strict convexity proves at most two, the all-zero coefficients are separately treated, and row elimination of the original delay characteristic matrix gives Δ(0)=μs(product a_i)F'(s). For F'<0, continuity and high-frequency positivity furnish a real λ>0. The eigenmode satisfies the biological integral history constraint. The two-root witness works for every n>=2 and parameters remain positive. Exact determinant and spectral spot checks corroborate the proof, but finite computation does not prove the universal claim.

originality.rationale: The primary source treats n general for existence, but proves complete coexistence multiplicity only for two common-latency phage types and exhibits instability numerically. The current all-finite-n sharp two-equilibrium classification, exact zero-frequency determinant identity, and guaranteed strictly positive real characteristic exponent are not stated or entailed by the inspected primary results. This conclusion is limited to searched/inspected works and does not certify historical uniqueness. A prior critical-dose law on the same equations is recognized: its coefficient κ matches F_s(0;α_c), but it addresses only local threshold dynamics, not this theorem’s global count or real characteristic index.
residual_risks: Specialized older delay-population stability results might supply a more general index theorem from which the zero-frequency sign could follow; a complete historical-priority proof is unavailable.
The Marchi et al. manuscript was not exhaustively read; its stated bacterial-resistance/immune model differs, but this is a bounded comparison.
Unseen publications and semantic-search recall limits could affect priority; lack of matches is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: At arbitrary cocktail size the cleared equilibrium equation can have degree n, but a structural strict-convexity argument forbids more than two feasible solutions and the bound is attained uniformly for every n. The analytic, delay-independent positive-real-characteristic-root certificate settles a natural dynamical distinction that previously appeared only numerically for two phages. Both the all-n complete positive-equilibrium census and the rigorous lower-branch instability are meaningful classification results for the published model rather than arbitrary parameter slices.
